scope: Descriptive worker-reported ROI means and 95% intervals. These are different anatomical averages of the same54 supplied maps, not independent study replications or an estimate of assistance effects. No pooled mean or equivalence claim. Primary inference used whole-brain correction, not these uncorrected descriptive intervals.

excerpt.quote: Within an independently defined vmPFC mask, the mean participant gain coefficient was −0.0078 (95% CI −0.0343 to 0.0187; 23/54 participant means were positive). This descriptive estimate is near zero and its interval includes zero. It is not a separate corrected test. The positive whole-brain voxels were posterior and do not localize to the hypothesized region.

excerpt.quote: The supplied gain-effect estimates do **not support a positive vmPFC response to potential gain** in the equal-indifference group. In an a priori 12 mm sphere centered at MNI (0, 40, -12), the mean participant effect was -0.0057 model units (95% CI [-0.0323, 0.0210]); the one-sided group test was *t*(53) = -0.43, *p* = .664. No voxel in the sphere survived whole-brain correction. A positive conclusion is not warranted by the small posterior signal found elsewhere in the brain.

excerpt.quote: To make vmPFC localization explicit without replacing the whole-brain test with an ROI test, we defined an anatomical sphere of 10-mm radius centered at MNI [0, 42, -8] mm, covering anterior medial orbitofrontal/vmPFC. The sphere was set independently of the group map and used for localization and descriptive summaries only. Its participant-averaged estimate was -0.0095 map units (SD=.103; 95% t interval [-0.0377, 0.0187]); the most positive voxel in the sphere had max-T adjusted p=1.00. The whole-brain corrected regions and the sphere are shown in Figure 1; Figure 2 shows the participant-level ROI values.

excerpt.quote: The supplied maps do **not support** a positive gain effect in vmPFC under whole-brain family-wise error (FWE) control. In 54 equal-indifference participants, no voxel in the prespecified vmPFC search zone survived one-sided permutation max-statistic correction (9,999 sign flips; minimum attainable p = .0001). The largest positive statistic inside that zone was *t*(53) = 4.19 at MNI [-2, 24, -18] mm, but its whole-brain FWE *p* was .778. The mean participant effect averaged over the search zone was -0.00010 (95% *t* interval [-0.01434, 0.01414], in upstream coefficient units).

Its peak vmPFC voxel was at (−2, 24, −13.2 mm; t = 2.34), with 0/1,297 vmPFC voxels passing max-t FWE at α = .05.

excerpt.quote: **We found no support for a positive gain-related response in the vmPFC.** In the predefined bilateral medial orbitofrontal ROI, the mean participant cope was −0.0079 (95% t interval −0.0346 to 0.0188; 54 participants; descriptive one-sided t = −0.60, p = .723). No whole-brain FWE-significant voxel overlapped the ROI. The whole-brain max-t test detected 24 positive voxels in three small posterior patches (26-neighbor connectivity used for description only; peak t = 6.62 at MNI [−26, −102, −3.6]; minimum corrected p = .00050). These posterior findings do not support the vmPFC hypothesis.

excerpt.quote: No positive vmPFC voxel survived whole-brain correction (0 of 6,174 mask voxels). The descriptive mean participant estimate within the mask was −0.0103 (95% t interval −0.0290 to 0.0084; t(53) = −1.10; one-sided p = .862); 21 of 54 participant averages were positive. Leave-one-participant-out ROI means ranged from −0.0144 to −0.0076. These data do not support the predicted positive vmPFC response.

excerpt.quote: All 54 participant maps passed checksum, geometry, and finite-value checks; there were no exclusions. The descriptive mean effect in the vmPFC coordinate box was −0.0022 map units (between-participant SD 0.071; 95% t interval for the mean [−0.0215, 0.0172]). The interval spans zero and the mean is close to zero. The whole-mask participant average was −0.0070 map units (95% t interval [−0.0215, 0.0075]); this is descriptive and does not replace voxelwise inference. Both summaries use supplied normalized-modulator estimates, not effects per currency unit. A post-selection check at the voxel with the largest observed vmPFC-box t statistic found t(53) = 4.19, uncorrected one-sided p = 5.3 × 10⁻⁵, but max-t FWE p = .791. Selecting the maximum within the box makes the uncorrected value optimistic; the corrected result does not support a regional claim. As a sensitivity analysis, voxelwise Bonferroni correction identified 11 positive voxels across the brain and zero in vmPFC, consistent with the primary max-t result.

This interval is compatible with small negative and positive average effects; it is not an equivalence test and does not establish a zero effect.
